page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs powered by 8 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES cryptography, and FMA. The instance provides no attached local SSD storage or integrated GPUs, relying on remote network attached storage, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate multi-core processing performance alongside lower single-core throughput. Single-threaded metrics, including a stress-ng single-core score of 1310.79 and a gzip compression speed of 22.94 GB/sec, fall in the lower quartile of tested cloud hardware. In contrast, multi-threaded benchmarks demonstrate consistent middle-tier capacity, characterized by a stress-ng multi-core result of 13967.71, a PassMark CPU score of 15413.0, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7270.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 781.7 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 86.1 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Real-world application tests record 13.56 million operations per second for Redis SET workloads and 11.54 GB/sec throughput for static web serving.

The ecs.c6e.4xlarge presents architectural tradeoffs between per-core speed and multi-core density. Because memory is capped at 2.0 GB per vCPU and single-thread execution speed is limited, the instance offers optimal qualitative resource efficiency for parallelized processing tasks rather than single-threaded or memory-bound workloads. Recommended workload deployments include web application frontends, multi-threaded compilation tasks, Redis in-memory caching nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed batch processing routines.
